subject: Dedicated reservation options and ramp plan — HavenBio (next steps)

Cc: procurement@havenbio.com

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial requirements

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. We ran the prototype through a few internal scenarios and we need a clear dedicated-reservation proposal to take to procurement. High-level asks:

- Production workload: always-on inference for two transformer families (a 13B variant for lower-latency fanout and a 70B quantized model for high-quality completions).
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions (average), with spiky peaks up to ~400 concurrent sessions during batch research windows.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 450ms for the 13B path; 99th percentile under 1.2s for the 70B path.
- Typical request size: 60–300 tokens output, average prompt prefix 200 tokens; top-k sampling.
- Retention/compliance: model inputs stored for 30 days for debug (we'll share SOC2 questions separately).

Can you send 2–3 concrete reservation options (cluster size, minimum guaranteed GPUs, ramp schedule over 6 months, estimated warmup/prewarm credits and canary approach) plus a rough cost delta between them? Procurement also asked for an expected activation timeline and what DocuSign / SOW steps you need.

I've attached a workload snapshot and our SLA requirements. If you want to pair on a short call tomorrow to review, I can do 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, very helpful. Below are three pragmatic reservation bundles that balance cost, reliability, and ramp flexibility. I’m keeping the high-level assumptions explicit so procurement has something tangible to review.

ASSUMPTIONS
- 70B model will be served quantized (8-bit/QLoRA-style flow) with constant KV cache size per active session.
- Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but we still maintain latency SLOs using dynamic batching windows.
- Burst capacity = on-demand shared pool that can be used for short spikes; pricing and latency vary.

OPTION A — Safety Floor (low commitment)
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 12 (A100-equivalent)
- Typical cluster size provisioned: 16 GPUs (12 guaranteed + 4 burst)
- Ramp schedule: Month 0–1: 12 GPUs; Month 2–3: +4 GPUs on 30% usage trigger; Month 4–6: review and add up to +8 GPUs if sustained throughput > 60%
- Prewarm credits: 200k tokens/month to seed KV cache during onboarding
- Canary plan: 1 node (2 GPUs) prewarm for 72 hours before cutover
- Suitability: teams wanting limited upfront OPEX and easy escape
- Notes: Lower unit price than on-demand, but higher tail-latency risk under heavy spikes

OPTION B — Balanced Onramp (recommended)
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 24
- Typical cluster size: 32 GPUs (24 guaranteed + 8 burst)
- Ramp schedule: Month 0: 24; Month 1: +4; Month 2: +4 (target 32 by month 2) — auto-scale policies allow temporary burst beyond 32 if negotiated
- Prewarm credits: 500k tokens/month, includes warm-start training window for prompt caches and rerankers
- Canary plan: 2-node canary (4 GPUs) with traffic shadowing for 14 days
- Suitability: production workloads with regular growth and tighter latency targets

OPTION C — Performance-First (higher commitment)
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 48
- Typical cluster size: 56 GPUs (48 guaranteed + 8 hot spare)
- Ramp schedule: immediate 48, steady-state; review at month 3 for vertical scaling to 64 if 70B usage > 70%
- Prewarm credits: 2M tokens/month and dedicated warmup window (48h) before each major release
- Canary plan: rolling canary across AZs, automated warm caches
- Suitability: latency-sensitive, heavy research bursts, enterprise SLAs

PRICING / CONTRACTING NOTES
- We’ll provide per-GPU unit rates and a tiered discount schedule in the formal proposal.
- Reserved minimums are contractual (monthly billing) with quarterly check-ins; we can include a 60-day exit window for Option A and B as a compromise.

NEXT STEPS
1) If any of these maps to HavenBio's procurement appetite, we’ll convert to a one-page SOW + pricing sheet.
2) Karthik and I can prepare a simple activation runbook (canary steps, prewarm playbook, rollback) and a DocuSign-ready SOW.
3) Book 30 minutes tomorrow at 10:15am PT for a call? If that works we’ll bring the deployment and finance leads.

I attached a short PDF that summarizes the three options.

Thanks — Mina

Alex, quick technical addendum to Mina's options so you have the numbers behind our recommendations. High-level throughput per GPU is model- and pipeline-dependent; below are conservative capacity estimates to size for your 13B/70B mix.

BASIS
- 13B (float16 inference, optimized kernels): ~26–32 synchronous requests/s per A100-equivalent GPU at your 95th-latency target with batching window tuned to 15–30ms.
- 70B (quantized 8-bit, KV-cache heavy): ~6–9 requests/s per GPU for the full-context runs you described.

SIMPLE SIZING MATH (steady-state baseline)
- Assume 70% of active sessions use 13B path, 30% use 70B. With 120 steady concurrent sessions: 84 sessions on 13B, 36 on 70B.
- Required GPUs (13B): 84 sessions / 30 reqs/s per GPU ≈ 2.8 GPU-equivalents (but concurrent behavior and variance → pad by 3–4x for headroom)
- Required GPUs (70B): 36 sessions / 8 reqs/s per GPU ≈ 4.5 → pad for KV memory and spike safety → 12 GPUs recommended for 70B workload

RECOMMENDATION TRANSLATED TO OPTIONS
- Option A: the 12-GPU floor maps mostly to guaranteeing the 70B latent capacity and relying on burst for short 13B patterns; not ideal for sustained 13B traffic.
- Option B (balanced): 24 guaranteed GPUs provides practical headroom: ~12 GPUs for 70B, ~8–10 for 13B steady, and buffer for autoscale.
- Option C: 48 GPUs gives comfortable headroom for both families and large research windows.

OPERATIONS NOTES
- Autoscale thresholds: trigger scale-out at 60% GPU utilization sustained for 90s; scale-in after 10 minutes below 40% utilization to avoid thrash.
- Warm caches: we recommend a nightly keep-alive job for long-tail KV-heavy sessions to reduce cold-start penalties.
- Fallback model: keep a quantized 30B-ish variant in the shared burst pool so heavy tails can be routed to a compatible lower-SLA but cheaper model if needed.

I’ll join the call if you want to walk the math live.
- Karthik

Karthik Iyer
